To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the generation and use of insight requires a value alignment and value-monitoring process across the insight demand-chain, and within firms, requires a customer insight conduct process including insight format, automation and insight sheperding.

the effective management of customer insight is a process that involves the alignment of value across multiple actors, and that it requires the conduct of customer insight in ways that facilitate the use of insight in decision making.
customer insight generation and use is a process of value alignment and monitoring, conducted in the form of insight shepherding and insight format, and supported by automation and other means.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processes of customer insight generation and use, which we define as the process by which organisations generate customer insight and then apply that insight in their marketing decisions.
the generation of customer insight, its transfer and its use.
how customer insight is generated and used in marketing decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study shows that the generation and use of insight is a complex and dynamic process, which is affected by a variety of factors and is not a straightforward matter of simply disseminating information.
this research has shown that customer insight is not a single entity but a collection of many types of insight, and that it is generated and used in a variety of ways.
the generation and use of insight is not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new framework to help managers understand the processes that they need to put in place to ensure that their organisation can generate, share and use customer insight in order to make better decisions.
we are not as good at generating and using insights as we think we are.

customer insight is a complex phenomenon that can be understood by considering its generation and use in a demand chain context, and the role of the organisation in shaping the demand chain and the insight it generates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the value of insight is not only in its content but also in the way it is generated and used within the firm.
the generation and use of insight requires a focus on the demand chain as well as on the process.
customer insight is more than a process and that its value is enhanced by the way that it is generated, used and shared.
